claims.text: The target alloy can be represented by an equiatomic Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 quinary composition.
The target Ta-based alloy is a single-phase BCC solid solution near melting.
The melting temperature of the target Ta-based alloy exceeds 1250 °C.
Standard experimental melting-property measurements are infeasible for the target system.
DFT thermodynamic integration is prohibitively expensive for this multicomponent alloy.
Classical EAM potentials fail to capture the complex liquid structure and give inaccurate multicomponent free-energy differences.
An MTP for a refractory alloy can be trained on DFT data from elemental, binary, ternary, and quaternary subsystems.
The MTP formalism offers a favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost.
An MTP captures the complex liquid structure of the target alloy better than EAM.
Explicit inclusion of high-temperature liquid configurations is required for reliable application to the quinary liquid.
A cutoff radius greater than 10 Å is sufficient or necessary to capture liquid-state coordination changes.
The relevant melting range for the target Ta-based alloy is approximately 2000–2500 K.
In CoCrFeMnNi, the magnetic states of the FCC and HCP phases are similar, with the Ni moment differing by less than 0.005 μB.
Similar magnetic states across phases reduce the magnetic-entropy contribution to their free-energy-related difference.
The magnetic moment distribution in a Ta-based refractory BCC alloy has low variance between solid and liquid states.
The magnetic entropy difference between the BCC solid and liquid or competing phases of the target alloy is negligible.
Magnetic-state similarity permits the magnetic-entropy integration step to be bypassed without materially degrading the target free-energy difference.
The proposed MTP perturbation method will predict melting temperature and solid-liquid free-energy differences within 5% of DFT thermodynamic-integration results.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by more than 90%, changing the runtime per composition from weeks to hours.
Strong changes in magnetic ordering between solid and liquid phases would invalidate the magnetic-state-similarity approximation.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies an MTP explicitly augmented with liquid configurations and trained across elemental through quaternary subsystems, whereas the uncertainty discusses extrapolation by a model trained on solid-state and binary data without explicit liquid configurations. That uncertainty addresses a materially different training protocol from the proposed intervention.
